sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Broadband Cellular Routers and Optical Terminals

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United Kingdom Trade and Investment Treaty (retained post-Brexit)
Egypt-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1992)
Egypt-European Union Association Agreement (2001, entered into force 2004)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering as amended by Law No. 78 of 2003, Law No. 181 of 2008, Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 8 of 2022; Executive Regulations adopted thereunder and as amended by Cabinet Decree No. 100 of 2020; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Regulations and directives of the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copy of Passport of Each Incorporator and Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or other competent authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through the originating state's foreign ministry; where the originating state is not party to the Apostille Convention, consular legalization by the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in that state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Existence and Good Standing of Each Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or corporate register in the shareholder's jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable in the jurisdiction of the issuing entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution of Each Foreign Corporate Shareholder Approving Formation of the Egyptian LLC and Appointing the Local Incorporation Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction and, if the shareholder is a corporate entity, its corporate secretary or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization by the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Source of Funds Declaration for the Investment Capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The remitting bank of record in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank attestation followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization in the jurisdiction of the issuing bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening of all incorporators, directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners against the Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Unit domestic blacklist, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT List, and Egypt's domestic anti-terrorism lists. Because the business scope is classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced under the ISIC 2630 telecom equipment OEM classification, screening must be completed prior to name clearance and re-run immediately before commercial registration and licensing by the National Telecom Regulatory Authority; positive hits require frozen-file escalation and obligatory filing of a suspicious transaction report with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop and Electronic Commercial Registry via the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones Business Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name must be in Arabic script and must comply with the Arabic commercial name format for a Limited Liability Company. The Latin-script transliteration is auxiliary, must be a faithful reverse transcription of the registered Arabic name, and must not conflict with any registered name similarity search. The name must not contain words that mislead the public or imply governmental sponsorship, military, religious-sectarian, or unlicensed financial activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the incorporator may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 15 working days of the rejection notice, attaching the official name-search report and a legal memorandum addressing the cited grounds. The committee must decide within 10 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may either submit a freshly amended name and repeat the reservation cycle or file a challenge before the Administrative Judicial Court on jurisdictional grounds. The original application fee is not refunded, and no appeal extension is granted after the 15-working-day deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office is mandatory for an Egyptian LLC. Virtual mail-forwarding services are accepted only as auxiliary administrative support and cannot satisfy the registered-office requirement. Because the target activity is Manufacture of Broadband Cellular Routers and Optical Terminals, GAFI and the National Telecom Regulatory Authority require a bookable manufacturing or warehouse address in an authorized industrial zone or a commercial-substance office; a purely virtual office is not sufficient for the statutory license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high; estimated at 45% probability of unannounced physical inspection within the first 18 months by GAFI commercial-registry inspectors and the National Telecom Regulatory Authority for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced telecom-equipment manufacturer. A lower-likelihood profile of under 10% would apply only to purely sales-oriented service LLCs without physical manufacturing substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, Book Three; amended by Law No. 4 of 2018; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Executive Regulations of Investment Law No. 1052 of 2018.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop-Shop and Commercial Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Arabic: Aqd Al-Ta'sis) executed before a notary public and filed with GAFI
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for an LLC under Companies Law 159/1981. The capital is set by the members in the Articles and must be fully subscribed. Contributions in Egyptian pounds or foreign currency may be transferred into the company's Egyptian bank account; no escrow account is statutorily mandated for a non-free-zone LLC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: THAT the capital subscriptions set out in the Articles of Association are hereby accepted and the Subscribers are recorded as members holding quotas in the agreed proportions; THAT the registered office of the Company shall be established at the address set forth in the Articles and registered with GAFI and the Commercial Registry; THAT the directors named in the Articles are appointed to serve until the first ordinary general meeting; THAT [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each with authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements, obtain licenses, and make regulatory filings; THAT these resolutions take effect immediately upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register on the GAFI investor portal, submit the proposed Arabic and English company name, select limited liability company form and ISIC 2630 / NAICS 334220 scope, and obtain the name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
Passport copies of the proposed managers
Notarized power of attorney for the applicant agent
Board resolution of the foreign parent authorizing the Egypt LLC formation
Declaration of intended registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, immediately submit two alternative names or file an administrative appeal to GAFI's Legal Affairs Department; the standard GAFI correction procedure applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public Office; Egyptian consular notary for foreign-executed documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all quota holders or their lawful attorney sign the Arabic-language Memorandum and Articles before an Egyptian notary. Signatures executed abroad must be legalized by the Egyptian embassy/consulate and then attested by the relevant notary. The activity clause must expressly include manufacturing and assembly of broadband routers and telecom terminal equipment.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association drafted in Arabic
Notarized signatures or powers of attorney of all members
GAFI name reservation certificate
Passport or national identity copies of members and managers
Lease contract or letter of intent for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial defects may be cured by correcting the instrument and re-executing before the same notary; if a signer is unavailable, a court-approved attorney may execute under a valid power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation and Commercial Registry Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop and Commercial Registry Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation package through GAFI One-Stop-Shop, pay statutory fees, and obtain the incorporation decision. The One-Stop-Shop will transmit the registration to the Commercial Registry, Tax Authority, Labor Office, and Social Insurance Authority.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI incorporation application form
Bank certificate evidencing capital contribution
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Form 11 (Declaration of Board Notarized) / manager declarations
Name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises an inquiry, respond in writing within 10 working days. A rejected application can be remedied by correction or appealed to GAFI's Appeal Committee before seeking an administrative court remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) counters integrated with GAFI One-Stop-Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the company tax card, tax identification number, VAT registration as applicable, and payroll tax file. The ETA will issue the official tax card incorporating the commercial registry number.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
Tax registration application Form 110/111
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office lease contract
Manager passports and personal IDs
First board resolution appointing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the tax file contains missing or inconsistent data, submit a written correction request to the ETA; if the tax card is not issued, the GAFI One-Stop-Shop will escalate to the ETA's tax card department for expedited issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organizational Resolutions and Bank Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Managers and Egyptian commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first formal board meeting, adopt the pro-forma resolutions, and issue the bank mandate. The appointed CEO/CFO opens the corporate bank account and files the mandate for Swift/TT payment rails.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
Tax card
First board resolution
Passport copies of authorized officers
Bank account opening forms
Declaration of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable, a circular written resolution or validly appointed alternate under the Articles of Association cures the defect; banking documentation discrepancies are corrected and re-filed directly with the compliance department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Operating License and NTRA Type Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) Licensing Center and National Telecommunication Regulatory Authority (NTRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the industrial licensing application under the Industrial Development Law No. 15 of 2017 for the manufacture/assembly of broadband cellular routers. After IDA preliminary approval, obtain NTRA type approval for the 5G CPE radio equipment before commercial sale.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
Memorandum and Articles of Association reflecting industrial activity
Factory site plan, lease or ownership deed
Environmental initial screening form from EEAA
Civil Defense fire safety layout
Technical specifications and circuit/bill of materials for NTRA
Tax card and insurance policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, supply corrected technical/test reports within 30 days. IDA refusal may be challenged before the IDA Grievance Committee; unsatisfied parties may appeal to the Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Occupational Health and Civil Defense Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA); Ministry of Interior Civil Defense; Ministry of Manpower occupational health office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the environmental permit and civil defense fire safety certificate before operating. Register the workplace with the Ministry of Manpower for occupational safety and health; undergo the required inspections and pay final certification fees.
required_dossiers: EIA report or simplified scoping form as applicable
Wastewater and hazardous waste management plan
Civil Defense fire alarm and extinguisher inspection request
Building structural and load-bearing certificate for equipment
Occupational health and safety registration form
Material safety data sheets for soldering chemicals
Noise, lighting and ventilation measurement report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies identified in inspection reports must be remediated, then re-inspection is requested. Administrative refusal may be appealed to the relevant authority; sustained delay can be accelerated through the GAFI One-Stop-Shop complaint mechanism.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) in coordination with the National Telecommunication Regulatory Authority (NTRA) and the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License under Law No. 15 of 2017 and NTRA Equipment Type Approval for 5G wireless customer-premises routers

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B Medium Environmental Impact – Simplified Environmental Impact Assessment scoping report is required. A full Category C EIA is not required where the operation is limited to surface-mount assembly, testing, packaging, and non-hazardous final assembly.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 and its Executive Regulations: industrial wastewater must meet the applicable effluent limits for COD, BOD, TSS, and heavy metals; VOCs from soldering and reflow processes must be controlled and within the emissions limits established in the environmental permit; hazardous electronic waste and spent solder must be managed through licensed handlers and accompanied by manifest documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense certificate of fire safety issued after inspection of fire alarms, extinguishers, emergency exits and production-line protection; building structural load clearance certified for installed equipment and shelf storage; occupational health and safety clearance under the Ministry of Manpower covering ventilation, noise control, electrical safety and first-aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Arab Republic of Egypt. Official e-portals: www.eta.gov.eg (tax-card, TIN, e-filing), einvoice.invoice.gov.eg (central e-invoicing fiscal clearance), ereceipt.invoice.gov.eg (retail e-receipts). Foreign investment incorporation and one-stop-shop processing: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), www.gafi.gov.eg. Customs interface: Egypt Customs Authority via Nafeza/ACI systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the EG LLC before GAFI/commercial registry: legalize foreign shareholding and board documents, appoint a resident general manager, establish a registered office. (2) Within 30 days of commercial registration, submit the unified tax-registration application to the competent ETA district office, attaching the commercial registry extract, premises title or lease, municipality license, import/export registration, NTRA or telecom-manufacturing license (where applicable for ISIC 2630 equipment), and ID cards or powers of attorney of authorized signatories. (3) ETA issues a unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and tax card covering corporate income tax, VAT, stamp tax, and payroll registration; VAT registration is ex lege mandatory once annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000. (4) Enroll in the ETA e-invoicing platform, obtain API and identity credentials, and certify the ERP or billing engine for XML/JSON invoice clearance before first supply. (5) If the plant is licensed inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) or a GAFI free zone, the zone authority issues a special tax and customs code with distinct export procedures; Egypt is a unitary state, so no sub-national tax registration is required. Typical lead time: 2-6 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The LLC is a resident juridical person under Companies Law No. 159/1981 and Investment Law No. 72/2017; it is per se a corporate taxpayer under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 on worldwide income at the applicable CIT rate (currently 22.5% for juridical persons), with no pass-through or distribution deduction. Territorial_Scope nuance: foreign-currency and foreign PE profits of resident companies are creditable but subject to Egyptian tax; non-resident enterprises without an Egyptian PE are taxed only on Egyptian-source income, while a PE or branch is taxed on attributable Egyptian-source income at the same CIT rate. Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment is not default; it is available only by statutory license (e.g., SCZone or GAFI free-zone industrial registrations), and the tax-card classification remains a normal resident taxpayer until a zone exemption decision is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide a US-style check-the-box or elective hybrid-mismatch regime; LLC classification is fixed by law. Available statutory elections and options: (i) depreciation policy election for production machinery and telecom-manufacturing fixed assets (straight-line or accelerated subject to ETA approval); (ii) Investment Law No. 72/2017 incentive elections, including state-approved investment cost deductions and zone-based incentives for new industrial projects in designated governorates and economic zones upon GAFI approval; (iii) VAT input-credit recovery elections, including pro-rata and special allocation methods for mixed taxable or exempt activities; (iv) fixed statutory loss carry-forward of 5 years under Article 24 of Law 91/2005, with no group relief or consolidation election for LLCs; (v) general anti-abuse rules under Article 30 of Law 91/2005 permit ETA recharacterization of hybrid or avoidance structures, but no hybrid-mismatch corrective-election mechanism is enacted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67/2016 as amended by Law No. 1/2021, and Executive Regulations Decree No. 66/2017
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration when annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000 (Article 16, Law 67/2016); voluntary registration when annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 100,000; compulsory registration irrespective of turnover for importers, exporters, and economic-zone operators.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Universal e-invoicing mandate through the ETA central clearance platform (einvoice.invoice.gov.eg). Every VAT invoice must be generated as an XML/JSON file, digitally stamped by the ETA crypto-stamp (UUID + QR code), and submitted via API or an ETA-certified billing system for real-time fiscal clearance within 24 hours of issuance. Unstamped or non-cleared invoices are legally invalid for input-VAT recovery and export zero-rating. A separate B2C e-receipt system applies mandatorily to retail merchants and telecom or electronics sellers. New TIN holders receive e-invoicing credentials at registration; non-compliance triggers per-invoice fines, suspension of clearance credentials, and audit triggers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VAT zero-rating under Article 9, Law 67/2016 applies to physical exports of goods by a VAT-registered manufacturer or exporter to buyers outside Egypt on transfer of title at FOB or CIF point of exit; wireless 5G CPE routers (ISIC 2630) qualify as tangible exported goods. Cumulative conditions: (i) the export invoice is a valid ETA-cleared e-invoice; (ii) goods actually leave Egypt through an Egyptian customs port evidenced by an approved export declaration; (iii) export shipment occurs within one year from the date of supply; (iv) export proceeds are received in foreign currency in an Egyptian bank account within CBE repatriation deadlines; (v) input-cost documentation substantiates manufacturing cost and the refund set-off. Offshore services supplied to non-residents require separate service-specific analysis; supplier-consignment or sham export arrangements do not qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayan Shikan) with customs exit stamp and Nafeza/ACI matching record
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing international carriage to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Egyptian bank confirming receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA export-refund desks audit zero-rating claims by cross-matching e-invoice clearance data, customs export declarations, shipping manifests, and bank FX remittance records; warehousing, factory, and documentary inspections may be ordered. False, inflated, or sham export claims are treated as tax evasion and trigger: (i) retrospective clawback of the 0% rate and assessment of 14% VAT on the full invoice value; (ii) monthly late-payment surcharge at the CBE discount rate plus 2% (Article 27, Law 67/2016); (iii) evasion penalties of up to EGP 1 million plus imprisonment of up to 5 years (Article 78, Law 67/2016; Article 137, Law 91/2005); (iv) additional customs-fraud penalties, confiscation, and exporter blacklisting under Customs Law No. 207/2020; and (v) permanent loss of zero-rating and refund privileges and suspension from CBE export-proceeds facilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the sole monetary, foreign-exchange, and banking licensing authority under the Central Bank and Banking Sector Law No. 88 of 2003 (as amended) and the Foreign Exchange Law No. 194 of 2020. The CBE licenses authorized dealer banks, operates the interbank FX market, issues exchange-control circulars, approves treasury/derivative transactions, and enforces AML/CFT obligations under Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt adopted a market-determined, flexible exchange-rate regime in March 2024 under an IMF-supported program; the EGP trades freely through authorized dealer banks and is fully convertible for documented current-account transactions (trade, services, royalties, freight). Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment injections, shareholder loans, and profit repatriation, are convertible but require GAFI registration, audited financial statements, tax clearance, and CBE-compliant inward/outward purpose codes. Profit remittance requires board-approved distribution, statutory audit reports, and confirmation of no outstanding tax liabilities; the 2022-2023 repatriation queue has largely cleared but documentary review remains a period cost.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All goods-export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt within 90 calendar days from the shipment date (per CBE circulars under Foreign Exchange Law No. 194 of 2020) and credited to an account at a CBE-licensed authorized dealer bank. Exporters may lawfully retain 100 percent of proceeds in foreign-currency accounts at Egyptian banks or convert voluntarily on the interbank market; no fixed compulsory conversion-to-EGP ratio currently applies. Extension of the 90-day window requires CBE prior approval; services and free-zone exporters are partially exempt. Non-repatriation triggers import payment blocks, penalties under the Foreign Exchange Law, and possible suspension of FX dealing privileges.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Foreign-Currency Account and Trade Finance (LC)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. The CBE Payment Services Law No. 18 of 2019 and its licensing regulations prohibit unlicensed e-money or payment institutions from holding, clearing, or settling EGP on behalf of Egyptian resident entities. Offshore digital EMIs and virtual-account providers (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business) cannot issue Egyptian IBANs, cannot route EGP-denominated trade settlements, and cannot satisfy the statutory export-proceeds repatriation rule, which is satisfied only through CBE-licensed authorized dealer banks. Such EMIs may be used only as ancillary non-EGP collection vehicles outside Egypt; core treasury liquidity must remain onshore.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory. CBE AML/CFT rules under Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended; CBE AML Regulation No. 39 of 2022) and standard authorized-dealer bank policy require the LLC's General Manager, at least one authorized signatory, and all natural-person beneficial owners to attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank branch. Remote or video-verified opening is not permitted as the sole onboarding channel for a non-resident-owned operating company; video verification is accepted only as a supplement after the physical interview. Non-resident signatories must execute a power of attorney legalized/apostilled, with passport copies, corporate registry extracts, and proof of shareholder existence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% non-resident foreign ownership with an opaque upstream ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI incorporation and capital registration certificates; current Egyptian commercial registry extract; beneficial-ownership (BO) register under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and BO Disclosure Law No. 83 of 2016; notarized board resolution appointing signatories; shareholding structure chart with ID/passport copies; source-of-funds evidence for the initial equity injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Telecom/ICT product line (5G wireless CPE routers) flagged as dual-use technology subject to import/export licensing scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (NTRA) equipment authorization/type-approval; Egyptian Customs tariff classification (HS 8517.62) and ACI registration; commercial end-user declaration and no-embargo statement; product datasheets demonstrating non-military, commercial-grade networking equipment; ISO 9001 certificate; complete supplier and customer KYC files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border trade movement projected through a thinly capitalized single-purpose manufacturing LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed global supply and distribution agreements; purchase orders and proforma invoice trail; transport documents (B/L, AWB) matched against Egyptian Customs ACI filings; LC and contract ledger; audited or internally prepared financial statements; tax clearance certificate; 12-month treasury cash-flow forecast; payroll and social-insurance records evidencing local operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intercompany or third-party funding (e.g., shareholder loans) lacking a clear trade or treasury nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed loan and subordination agreements; CBE inward-remittance purpose code declarations; board-approved intercompany treasury policy; downstream procurement contracts confirming deployment into working capital; lender's source-of-funds bank statements; ledger reconciliation schedule linking each remittance to the LLC's accounting system.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed only through CBE-licensed authorized dealer banks using SWIFT MT103 messages. The instruction must carry the correct CBE inward-remittance purpose code for equity contribution/capital increase and reference the GAFI-approved subscription or capital increase resolution. The bank requires: (i) updated commercial registry extract reflecting the new capital; (ii) board resolution authorizing the issuance/allotment; (iii) shareholder subscription agreement and payment statement; (iv) GAFI filing confirmation; (v) tax card and account opening forms. Funds are credited to a designated capital-contribution collection account, held in USD or converted to EGP at the interbank rate, and released to the operational account only after GAFI and commercial registry registration evidence is delivered. Source-of-funds and BO verification precede any credit; the transaction is reported to the CBE through the bank's periodic FX and balance-of-payments filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All import disbursements for components and materials used in 5G CPE manufacturing must be executed through an authorized dealer bank using: (i) commercial letters of credit (issuance via SWIFT MT700; settlement via SWIFT MT103 upon conforming presentation); (ii) documentary collections (DP/DA) with the bank as collecting agent; or (iii) direct telegraphic transfer (MT103) where the beneficiary is a pre-approved supplier under the bank's trade facility and goods are cleared or contractually documented. The LLC must hold a current importer registration in the CBE importer registry, valid tax and importer codes, and file each consignment in the Customs ACI (Advance Cargo Information) system. Bank processing requires proforma invoices, transport documents, and, where applicable, NTRA import authorization; cash, cheques, and unregulated payment-service settlement are prohibited. Export proceeds from customers flow through the bank's export collection desk via MT103/LC, are captured on the export proceeds register, and monitored for the 90-day repatriation obligation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable EGP FX forwards (tenor matched to real trade/treasury exposure; CBE-approved underlying documentation and bank credit line required)
Non-deliverable EGP forwards (NDFs) booked with international counterparties to hedge depreciation risk without onshore settlement
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) executed through authorized dealer banks against documented economic exposure and CBE derivative reporting
Plain-vanilla FX options (limited onshore availability; quoted only with a verifiable real exposure and retained for trade-flow hedging)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Central Department of Income Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; calendar-year entities must file by 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 2% per month on the unpaid tax (capped at 50%); fixed penalty of EGP 2,000 for late filing, increasing to EGP 5,000 for continued failure, plus criminal prosecution and 3-year discovery statute of limitations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry – Ministry of Trade and Industry (executed through GAFI for corporate entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during January for the current calendar year; grace period normally secured through payment of late surcharge until 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge in increasing amounts (EGP 200–500); prolonged non-renewal triggers administrative strike-off from the commercial register, loss of juridical standing and criminal sanctions for operating without valid registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Local Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually; tax cards expire on 31 December and renewal applications are accepted in January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of EGP 500; non-renewal may cause the company to be placed on ETA non-compliant list, blocking customs, bank transfers and many public tender operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Ordinary General Assembly Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) / Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary General Assembly must be held within 4 months of fiscal year end; ratified audited financial statements must be filed with GAFI within 30 days after assembly approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EGP 500–2,000 per month of delay; repeated defaults may trigger disqualification of managers, loss of tax deduction for audit fees, and blocking of GAFI corporate services

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Egyptian LLCs regardless of turnover or asset thresholds under Companies Law 159/1981; no statutory exemption based on size exists for domestic LLCs, and the audit must be performed by a certified Egyptian auditor registered with the ETA under the Accounting and Auditing Law 194/2013.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Ministry of Investment, substantially converged with IFRS; public interest entities and regulated financial institutions follow additional CBE requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egyptian AML Law and Companies Law regulations require each LLC to maintain an up-to-date beneficial ownership register. There is no fixed annual UBO re-filing deadline; however, the register must be reconciled with the partners' register on each anniversary of incorporation, and every transfer of quotas or change in UBO must be reported to the Commercial Registry/GAFI within 30 days. A no-change declaration is recommended as good practice at the annual statutory meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes Book (General Assembly and Management Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–800 per year for basic Cairo/Alexandria registered office and legal agent; USD 500–1,200 for package with compliance secretarial services in GAFI zones.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,600–4,800 for a medium-size manufacturing LLC (ISIC 2630) with wireless CPE production; USD 8,000+ if consolidated, affiliated, or subject to transfer pricing documentation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard CIT rate for an Egyptian LLC is 22.5%. Investment incentives under Law No. 72 of 2017, with GAFI approval, may include a 50% deduction of permitted investment costs in targeted areas or industries, and Free Zone regimes can exempt exported telecom equipment profits for up to 10 years. No general patent box or R&D super-deduction applies to 5G wireless CPE manufacturing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 19 (Legal Persons) via the Egyptian Tax Authority's E-TAKTA e-filing portal (www.eta.gov.eg)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within four months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year LLC, the filing deadline is 30 April. Quarterly advance CIT payments are due within the last day of the month following each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, TIN, commercial register number, GAFI investment file number, and principal address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian PE/branch TIN; state ultimate parent jurisdiction and the authorised local manager's particulars.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period and business classification: start/end dates, ISIC activity code 2630, NAICS 334220, and a short description of 5G CPE router manufacturing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only Egyptian-source revenue; list required licenses (telecom equipment approval, customs free-zone license if used).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement fields: gross sales, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, non-operating income, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include revenues from physical sales made in/from Egypt and expenses effectively connected to the Egyptian PE. Head-office overhead is deductible only when recharged under a valid corporate-services agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction schedule and transfer pricing disclosure: value of intercompany purchases, sales, royalties, loans, management fees, and the arm's-length method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Egyptian TP disclosure statement; if related-party transactions exceed EGP 4,000,000 in aggregate, submit Local/Master File extracts with Form 19.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: taxable income after loss set-off, exemptions, available credits, and CIT at 22.5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty withholding tax credits only where the Egyptian source return has been made; include proof of TRC if a DTA relief is relied on.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts 2% per month of the tax due (minimum EGP 500), plus an administrative fine of EGP 2,000 to EGP 20,000 for record-keeping violations. Understatement of income can add up to 100% penalty on the evaded tax; deliberate concealment triggers criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Advance CIT Payment Voucher filed and paid through E-TAKTA's 'Advance Tax Payment' module
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly instalments are due by 30 April, 31 July, 31 October, and 31 January for a calendar-year taxpayer; each instalment is normally based on 25% of the final tax payable for the preceding tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select the tax year quarter for which the advance payment is tendered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers with a PE in Egypt must file through their authorised representative and quote the Egyptian TIN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the preliminary tax base by reference to the previous year's audited taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the previous year's Form 19 taxable profit, excluding foreign-source profits and branch remittance amounts not subject to Egyptian CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount paid: one-quarter of the prior year's total CIT liability, adjusted for any known permanent changes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bank remittances must reference the E-TAKTA voucher number; late payment is adjusted by the ETA with statutory credit and debit interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Unpaid advance instalments accrue monthly statutory credit interest (currently applied at 2% per month for delay), and the ETA may attach bank accounts or move to seizure without prior notice after the quarterly due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (outbound dividends from an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 5% under several Egyptian DTAs).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply an reduced treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the home jurisdiction, (ii) submit the TRC plus a beneficial-owner statement to the Egyptian paying LLC before the distribution, and (iii) ask the ETA for a technical approval via the E-TAKTA DTA relief workflow. If the Egyptian payer withholds at the statutory 10% because approval arrives late, the non-resident must file a Form 4 refund claim within five years from the end of the tax year of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Egyptian withholding tax on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 20%. Under Egypt's DTAs (e.g. UK, Germany, France, Italy) rates are frequently reduced to 10%–15% for royalties and 10%–15% for interest, subject to beneficial-ownership status and submission of the TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 4,000,000 aggregate controlled transactions trigger the mandatory Egyptian Local File; a Master File is additionally required where the MNE group's consolidated global turnover exceeds EGP 500,000,000. CbC reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EGP 25 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but Law No. 91 of 2005 and its TP rules impose an economic-substance test. A non-resident-owned LLC producing 5G CPE routers in Egypt must show real premises, technical staff, production records, inventory, and decision-making functions. The ETA may disregard or recharacterise a shell LLC that merely routes sales, and in such case, it will re-attribute profits to the foreign principal, impose penalties, and deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of Egyptian-sourced revenue from wireless router sales, recording fake commissions to offshore sister companies, falsifying invoices from Chinese/Emirati vendors, or omitting related-party royalty income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 91 of 2005 and Law No. 67 of 2016 (VAT/customs), conviction carries a penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax, fines of EGP 5,000–50,000, monthly interest, and imprisonment of between two and seven years; the ETA may reopen assessments for five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing directors and managers are jointly civilly liable for the evaded tax, interest and penalties; asset attachment, travel bans and custodial sanctions apply. The ETA will pierce the corporate veil if the LLC was operated as a mere conduit for tax avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Arm's-Length Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling 5G CPE routers to or from a related party at manipulated margins, absence of contemporaneous Local/Master File when the EGP 4,000,000 threshold is met, or submitting a site-specific file that does not support the tested party's risk and function profile.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will effect an arm's-length adjustment and impose a penalty of up to 30% of the additional tax (or more if concealment is proven), an administrative fine for no/insufficient TP documentation (up to EGP 100,000), and statutory late-payment interest on the adjusted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved non-arm's-length contracts without business substance or failed to instruct TP compliance can be made personally liable for the additional tax when the company cannot pay; travel bans may be issued during recovery proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Egyptian LLC only maintains a PO Box and a bank account, with operations, warehousing, engineering staff, and key decisions all physically located outside Egypt while inbound orders are booked as Egyptian sales to access treaty benefits or lower effective taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may disregard the legal personality of the LLC under anti-abuse rules, re-source the revenue to the foreign beneficial owner, assess a 100% evasion penalty, impose customs/VAT penalties on importation, and revoke the commercial registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and the local shareholder representative may be held jointly liable for the avoided tax, and criminal referral can be made for aiding a sham entity as an instrument of tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving or paying large cash sums above the Egyptian statutory threshold (EGP 500,000) without suspicious-transaction reporting, maintaining undisclosed beneficial ownership for the LLC's foreign parent, or routing 5G equipment revenue through private crypto wallets or unlicensed remittance houses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with Egypt's AML Law No. 80 of 2002 triggers fines, confiscation of the funds involved, and imprisonment of up to 15 years; the Financial Regulatory Authority may freeze bank accounts and cancel licences, while telecom trade licences become suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who have acted in bad faith or without due diligence face personal criminal exposure, confiscation orders, travel bans, and are barred from serving on future boards; extradition may be available under bilateral mutual legal assistance treaties.
